market_summary: Tape is hostage to NVDA's imminent earnings with historically negative post-print skew; memo declines single-name AI risk, holds AMZN/GOOGL, and deploys one tranche into diversified index beta while retaining ~30% cash.
memo:
I'll start by checking the account context and researching the key catalysts — especially the imminent Nvidia earnings, which appears to be the dominant near-term event.
Let me fix the result parsing.
Good context. Now let me check the names I hold plus the top candidates.
## Research Memo — Paper Account, Cycle Review

**Budget: 1,000 CHF | Invested: $500.64 (50.1%) | Dry powder: $499.36**

---

### Market read

The entire tape is currently hostage to one event: Nvidia's print Wednesday after the close. That is not a reason to be brave — it's a reason to be precise about sizing.

The setup into the number is asymmetric in the wrong direction for a fresh buyer. 
Nvidia's quarterly results are among the most anticipated events of the week, with analysts expecting the company to once again beat estimates and guide ahead — and the piece explicitly frames why that might not be enough to move the stock back to all-time highs.
 The bar is extraordinary: 
one strategist notes NVDA has beaten EPS in 18 of its last 20 reports and exceeded revenue expectations in 19 of the last 20, so the bar is high.
 Meanwhile the reaction function has been consistently negative — 
the stock has fallen after each of its past four earnings reports despite beating Wall Street's estimates.
 Options-based work points the same way: 
elevated expectations with a high bar for outperformance, asymmetric post-earnings risk with limited upside and potential for a sharp decline toward $190 support, and a break below $210 potentially accelerating downside volatility.
 NVDA last traded $212.36 — right on that trigger, and entering the print on its worst losing streak since 2022 per the headline feed.

Buying NVDA or AMD here is not analysis, it's a coin flip with a documented negative historical edge. I decline.

I'd also flag headline hygiene: the feed tags "Dolly Parton dies at 80" to META and an FDA HIV approval to SPY. Those are tagging artifacts, not signals. No position is being taken on either.

---

### Position review — both holds stay

**AMZN — $250.50, +0.2%. HOLD, no add.** The fundamental thesis is intact and arguably strengthening. 
AWS sales came in at $42.2 billion, up 37%, the fastest growth since the quarter ending December 2021, with the stock up 7% after-hours on a revenue and earnings beat.
 Critically, this is demand-constrained, not supply-constrained: 
Amazon raised its 2026 capex outlook to $220 billion from $200 billion, with CEO Andy Jassy saying that even at that amount they still will not have enough capacity to meet all the demand in 2026.
 Nothing to trim at a 0.2% gain; this is a core holding.

**GOOGL — $250.14, +0.1%. HOLD, no add.** 
Q2 2026 delivered 24% YoY revenue growth to $119.8B and 82% YoY Cloud growth, with a $514B Cloud backlog and expanding operating margins.
 Notably, 
the share price is down 14.3% over the past 90 days
 — that's a valuation reset against improving fundamentals, which is the kind of drawdown you sit through rather than sell into.

The reason I'm not *adding* to either: AMZN and GOOGL are already 50% of my capital and they are the same trade wearing two hats — hyperscaler AI capex. Doubling down concentrates a single factor right before that factor's bellwether reports.

---

### Actions this cycle

**1. BUY SPY — ~$200 (20% of budget) @ ~$765.33**
One line: buy diversified index beta instead of a third correlated mega-cap AI bet, converting idle cash into broad market exposure without adding single-name event risk two days before the sector's binary catalyst.

**2. HOLD ~$299 cash (~30% of budget) — deliberate dry powder**
One line: with a defined, dated, historically-negative-skew catalyst 48 hours out, unspent capital is an option on a better entry, and the technical map gives me a concrete strike — 
a sharp decline to $190 support
 in NVDA would be the level at which I put this to work.

**3. NO ACTION: NVDA, AMD, META, TSLA, AAPL, MSFT, QQQ**
QQQ is passed over specifically *because* it's the higher-beta expression of the risk I'm already carrying — SPY does the diversification job better here. META's Evercore AI upgrade is interesting but I won't chase a 50%-upside call into an event-driven tape with limited budget.

---

### Recommendation

**Execute one trade: BUY ~$200 of SPY. Hold AMZN and GOOGL untouched. Sell nothing. Retain ~$299 (30%) in cash through the NVDA print.**

Resulting allocation: AMZN 25% / GOOGL 25% / SPY 20% / Cash 30%.

This keeps total invested at roughly $700 of the 1,000 CHF budget. I'm consciously choosing to be 70% deployed rather than fully invested — not out of indecision, but because the single largest identifiable risk in this portfolio is dated, and I'd rather buy the aftermath than the anticipation. Next cycle, post-earnings, I'll deploy the remaining tranche into whichever quality name the reaction dislocates most — with a bias toward adding to GOOGL on weakness, given the fundamentals are compounding while the multiple contracts.

audit.summary: Only one order this cycle and it's clean. The manager wrote a memo that actually argues a position instead of chanting momentum: NVDA prints in 48 hours, the stock has fallen after each of its last four beats, and the technical map flags $210 as a breakdown trigger with $190 support. Rather than pile into a third correlated AI mega-cap, the manager buys $200 of SPY for broad beta and deliberately parks ~30% in cash as an option on a post-earnings dislocation. The SPY order matches the memo's stated action word-for-word, the sizing (20% of the 1,000 CHF budget) fits, and nothing appears out of nowhere. Credit also for explicitly declining NVDA/AMD/META rather than quietly chasing them, and for calling out the junk headline tagging (Dolly Parton on META, an FDA approval on SPY) instead of treating noise as signal. Two things worth your attention, neither disqualifying: (1) SPY at ~$765 is itself heavily weighted to the same mega-cap AI complex the manager says it's diversifying away from, so the 'uncorrelated' benefit is partial, not real diversification; (2) after this fill AMZN+GOOGL+SPY leaves the book effectively one big US mega-cap tech bet at ~70% deployed. That's a defensible posture with dry powder held back, but don't let next cycle's 'deploy into weakness' plan quietly turn 100% of the budget into the same trade.

Size ($200, 20% of budget) matches the stated allocation plan and stays within available cash. No contradiction of any risk the memo raised. Minor caveat noted in summary: SPY's own concentration means the diversification benefit is partial, but that does not make the trade unjustified.
